reason: Attacked and it holds on wording and attribution; the locator is right in substance but is hung on the one edition that cannot show it, so the source line should be amended. WORDING: read in Ruskin’s own text twice over. The Project Gutenberg text of Unto This Last and Other Essays on Political Economy (ebook 36541) prints, in the closing paragraph of the fourth essay, “I desire, in closing the series of introductory papers, to leave this one great fact clearly stated. THERE IS NO WEALTH BUT LIFE. Life, including all its powers of love, of joy, and of admiration.” The scan of the 1862 Smith, Elder first edition (archive.org, ruskinuntothislast) prints the same sentence in display capitals at the same place. The shipped line is that sentence entire, cut at Ruskin’s own full stop, with nothing added and nothing moved; setting Ruskin’s display capitals as an ordinary sentence is normalisation, not minting. LOCATOR, THE GOOD HALF: section 77 is correct. Two numbered editions were read to check it, archive.org untothislastfour01rusk (Thomas Y. Crowell, New York, introduction by Richard T. Ely) and untothislastfour1901rusk, and both print 77. at the head of the paragraph that begins “It is, therefore, the manner and issue of consumption which are the real tests of production” and that runs on to the sentence in question, under the running head AD VALOREM. LOCATOR, THE DEFECT: the 1862 Smith, Elder first edition carries NO section numbers at all. In that scan the paragraph is unnumbered and the cross reference to sections 40 and 41 that the later numbered editions print is simply absent from the 1862 text. So “section 77 (Smith, Elder, 1862)” asks a reader to find in the first edition an apparatus the first edition does not have. The honest source either drops the publisher and keeps the section, which is how every numbered edition can be followed, or keeps 1862 and cites a page. EVIDENCE OVERSTATED, though the line survives it: the verifier’s cited URL, quikscan.org/UTL, is a QuikScan presentation, a modernised restatement with its own numbered summary points, and at one place it prints “7. My key point is this: THERE IS NO WEALTH BUT LIFE. That country is richest that produces the...”, which is a paraphrase of Ruskin and not Ruskin. The evidence claim that this page is a complete online edition read with the surrounding paragraph intact, and that it confirmed the standard section numbering, is not what that page is or does. The section number was confirmed here against the numbered printings instead. ATTRIBUTION: Ruskin, and no trap on the misattribution list touches it. SCOPE: the four essays ran in the Cornhill Magazine from August to November 1860 and were collected by Smith, Elder in 1862, so it is pre-1999, a named work by a named author, and it is not scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business writing or oratory. TAG: Essay is the form of the work, which is four essays. FORM: the source leads with the author’s name, carries no dash and no straight double quote, and runs 116 characters against the 140 cap.
